title: Starter Code Template Builder
description: Create a fixed starter template in one of six supported languages. Your label names the example; requested behavior is not implemented.
intro: Starter Code Template Builder selects a fixed template for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, or SQL. A short label changes a name or comment. It does not understand a requested feature or implement it: the template remains a starting point that you must edit and test.
audience: Developers and learners who want a small, editable language starter
input: A short template label, such as order handler, and one of the six supported target languages shown in the selector.
outcome: A fixed starter example with a name or comment derived from the label; application-specific behavior still needs to be implemented.
review: Read the entire template before using it. The example does not implement the label, validate a business requirement, or include your project dependencies.
bestFor: Beginning a small practice file or scratch example when a fixed template is sufficient and you plan to write the behavior yourself.
steps: Choose JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, or SQL.
Enter a short label used to name or annotate the template.
Choose Create Template and inspect the fixed example in the output panel.
Download the text, add your required logic, and compile or test it in your own project.
useCases: Starting a TypeScript scratch function with a label you recognize.
Creating a Python practice file to edit locally.
Comparing the shapes of small JavaScript and Go starter examples.
Preparing a SQL query skeleton before choosing real tables, fields, and conditions.
commonMistakes: Writing a feature request and expecting an implementation of that request.
Assuming the starter has been compiled against your project.
Copying the sample unchanged into production without adding the required behavior.
tips: Use a label rather than a multi-paragraph feature request.
Replace the sample pass-through behavior with your implementation.
Add imports, types, and tests required by your actual environment.
SQL templates require you to replace example table and column names.

faq.question: Does a natural-language request become working code?
faq.answer: No. Each supported language has a fixed template. The supplied label changes only names or comments, not program logic.

faq.question: Which languages have a starter?
faq.answer: The builder offers JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, and SQL templates. Other language targets are unavailable.

faq.question: Why does the generated function return its input?
faq.answer: The pass-through example is intentional scaffolding. You must replace it with the desired behavior and add tests.

faq.question: Is this connected to an AI model?
faq.answer: No model is connected. Template selection and label formatting happen locally in your browser.

faq.question: Does the download have the target language extension?
faq.answer: The builder downloads starter-template.txt. Choose the appropriate file extension and project layout when you save it in your own development environment.
